plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lilac-pink goblets rise straight from bare soil, with no leaves in sight. They carpet damp meadows and woodland edges just as autumn begins.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (roughly September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland clearings across central and western Europe, including the UK, Germany and France
plants.funFact: The leaves appear in spring and die back by summer. The flowers then emerge months later, which earned the plant the nickname 'naked ladies'. All parts are toxic, and the plant is the natural source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: Dense clusters of daisy-like flowers with violet rays and golden centers blaze along roadsides and prairies. They are a late-season feast for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Meadows, prairies and wet fields across eastern and central North America
plants.funFact: Its blooms are a critical late-season nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies. The flower heads also close up on cloudy days and at night.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: This tree is covered in lavender-blue trumpet flowers before its leaves fully return. Streets and parks in the southern hemisphere spring are washed in purple, and fallen petals carpet the ground below.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (October to November in the southern hemisphere)
plants.location: Pretoria and Johannesburg in South Africa, and parts of Australia such as Brisbane and Sydney
plants.funFact: Native to South America, the jacaranda has become a symbol of spring in Pretoria, often called the 'Jacaranda City'. Its blooming is so closely tied to exam season in Australia and South Africa that students have a saying about it.
